title: BlackRock Warns of Recession if Data Centers Stall; Morgan Stanley Vows Continued AI Investment
key_facts: Larry Fink, BlackRock CEO, told CNBC on 14 Oct 2026 that a data-centre moratorium would put the US in recession.
SBS says he spoke after BlackRock's third-quarter earnings and called BlackRock the world's largest asset manager.
Brookings says more than 100 localities and at least 15 states have considered or adopted data-centre restrictions.
New York imposed a statewide pause on new hyperscale facilities in 2026.
Data Center Watch counts at least 75 US data-centre projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026.
Fink says the build-out is filling a shortage of electricians, plumbers and welders.
Yahoo notes Fink's firm has significant holdings in technology and infrastructure.
quote_evidence: "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," BlackRock CEO Larry Fink told CNBC on October 14, 2026.
That is his warning, not a consensus economic forecast, and the distinction matters.
why_it_matters_hint: Local limits on data centres are spreading, and Fink argues they could cost the whole economy.
notes: SBS item; Morgan Stanley part unverified.
